Data:Slnev.visiting.denzil.morgen.json.startdescription: Morgen disdains Denzil. He, in his turn, keeps a respectful distance, and can be observed to scratch a sun-cross covertly into the table when she's not looking.

Data:Slnev.visiting.denzil.olympe.json.startdescription: Olympe chats to Denzil about village life. It is mostly Olympe who does the chatting.

Data:Slnev.visiting.denzil.serena.json.startdescription: Denzil and Serena reminisce about her time as Librarian, and the weeks the younger Denzil spent up at Hush House, helping repair the foundry, after he quarrelled with his father… and before he went off to war.

Data:Slnev.visiting.denzil.stanislav.jso.startdescription: Stanislav solicitously advises Denzil on a poultice for his lumbago. [Lesson: Herbs & Infusions]

Data:Slnev.visiting.denzil.yvette.json.startdescription: Denzil's eyes widen at the sight of Yvette. He inclines his head respectfully , but barely responds to any of her questions.

Data:Slnev.visiting.denzil.zachary.json.startdescription: It seems that Denzil and Zachary know each other from the time that Zachary spent recuperating in Brancrug after the Great War. They speak of the paths they have not taken. Denzil has never married, nor been further south than Ypres. Zachary has not touched a gun since the War, nor ever returned to the place of his birth. [Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.agdistis.json.startdescription: Mrs Kille and Agdistis greet each other warmly. It seems they knew each other in Paris, in the days before they married. She asks about his dance school… [Lesson: Drums & Dances]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.aladim.json.startdescription: Al-Adim and Mr Kille discuss the birds of prey that haunt the moors. Mr Kille is intrigued to learn of al-Adim's interest in falconry, though he has never practised it himself. [Lesson: Furs & Feathers]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.arthur.json.startdescription: Arthur and Mr Kille discuss some of the more ghastly wounds they have seen on corpses. Their various professional interests lead them astray, and they both go quiet after a sharp glance from Mrs Kille reminds them where they are. [Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.arun.json.startdescription: Arun exercises his charm to overcome Mr Kille's wariness of foreigners. He describes his 'skin condition' in elliptical terms, and invites advice from Mr Kille on how it might be better concealed. Mr Kille insists that he is a coffinmaker, not an embalmer, but has a suggestion or two nevertheless... [Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.azita.json.startdescription: Azita and Mrs Kille exchange weather-lore. ('Plenty of babies shy of birth, can't wait to stick their heads out in a storm' opines Mrs Kille gloomily.) [Lesson: Sky Stories]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.chaima.json.startdescription: Chaima and Mr Kille discuss funerary customs across Europe and beyond. [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.connie.json.startdescription: Connie questions Mrs Kille about stories of changelings in the remoter parts of the county. Mrs Kille insists that these are only stories… but admits she has been known to string windowsills with red thread, and place rowan twigs beneath the cradle, just in case. [Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.coquille.json.startdescription: Coquille and Mrs Kille discuss means to ease childbirth, and to prevent it. [Lesson: Orchids & Narcotics]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.corso.json.startdescription: Corso hauls his notebook from his pocket and displays a magazine clipping: 'Subtle Earth', a poem he enjoyed, written by none other than Mr Kille. Mr Kille, embarrassed, leans in close to discuss it. He admits that conversations in the Sweet Bones with the more memorable visitors to Hush House provided inspiration... [Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.dagmar.json.startdescription: Dagmar greets Mrs Kille as 'Mlle Raveline', corrects herself, thumps her on the shoulder, asks about various French relatives of Mrs Kille's that Mrs Kille hasn't seen in years, enthuses about various other French relatives of Mrs Kille's that Mrs Kille hasn't seen in years, and eventually asks if she's had any trouble with 'la malaise raveline'. Mrs Kille answers politely that she has not... but that she has chosen not to have children, just in case. Across the table, Mr Kille catches her eye with the familiarity of long marriage and reaches for her hand.

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.douglas.json.startdescription: Douglas is commissioning a very particular coffin from Mr Kille: lightning-struck wood, copper bands (which Mr Kille says doubtfully that he hopes Denzil can do) and the whole not to be allowed to touch the earth before Douglas takes delivery… [Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.ehsan.json.startdescription: Mrs Kille and Ehsan discuss the binding and suturing of wounds. [Lesson: Stitching & Binding]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.fraser.json.startdescription: Fraser asks Mrs Kille whether there have been any unusual births in the countryside hereabouts of late - animals, or humans? She admits that yes, there have. He asks if any of them have featured wings, or unusual eyes? After a longer pause, she says that yes, some have, but she knows of none that have survived. [Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.hokobald.json.startdescription: Mr and Mrs Kille sit as far away from Hokobald as possible. Neither of them will look at him.

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.morgen.json.startdescription: Mrs Kille respectfully addresses Morgen as Chaculette - a title that Morgen seems to recognise - and bows her head. Morgen touches a finger to her lips, and then to Mrs Kille's forehead - perhaps a blessing, perhaps something else. There is a pause, after which Morgen begins a casual account of a recent sea voyage. [Lesson: Sea Stories]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.olympe.json.startdescription: Mr Kille and Olympe are enthusing about Noël Coward, of whom, it seems, they are both enthusiastic admirers. Olympe mentions that she has, packed carefully away inside her luggage, a 78 disc with Coward's most recent work, 'Don't Put Your Daughter On the Stage, Mrs Worthington', and offers to lend it to Mr Kille, who is so excited that he almost kicks over his chair. [Lesson: Strings & Songs]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.serena.json.startdescription: Serena knew Mr Kille when he was an 'untidy youth'. They reminisce about Brancrug just after the War; then she reminds him of the time he got caught scrumping in the Practic Garden, and though he laughs with her, the tone turns awkward, and the conversation ends shortly afterwards.

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.stanislav.jso.startdescription: Stanislav asks Mrs Kille if the old tradition is still practiced in Brancrug; if mothers still leave infants to sleep overnight in the roots of an apple tree. Mrs Kille flashes her brief, melancholy smile and acknowledges that yes, it is sometimes still done; but most mothers pay Mrs Kille to do it for them, so they don't get in trouble with Reverend Timothy; and that she always stays out overnight to watch the infant, which is not necessarily what was done in the times before the Church. [Lesson: Rites of the Roots]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.yvette.json.startdescription: Yvette has heard from Corso of Mr Kille's tendency to poetry. She asks him about his inspirations, and he shares them, albeit cautiously. She asks him about his dreams, and he glances around, then puts a finger to his lips. 'Not in the House,' he says. [Lesson: Sights & Sensations]

Data:Slnev.visiting.killes.zachary.json.startdescription: Zachary confides to Mrs Kille that he thinks he will eventually be delivered of 'a kind of child'. He asks if she can help. She scrutinises him; and says quietly that she cannot. He asks if she thinks he will live through the birth; she considers for a long time, and then says more quietly that she thinks that he will. He asks, last, when she thinks the child might be born: she leans in close and whispers, 'I think on a midsummer's day.'  [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.agdistis.jso.startdescription: Agdistis expresses an interest in Ericapaean. Reverend Timothy, who has not been initiated into the higher mysteries of the Church, professes himself 'very far from fluent' in it, but is happy to share a few pointers. [Lesson: Ericapaean]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.aladim.json.startdescription: Timothy and al-Adim discuss al-Jabal, 'the sun rising over the mountain' - the Syrian god with whom the notorious emperor Elagabalus notoriously identified himself. They speak, too, of the Emesan cult that honours god and emperor still - to Timothy's clear if furtive fascination. [Lesson: Sand Stories]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.arthur.json.startdescription: Reverend Timothy is in possession of a manuscript on ink-mixing that he proudly believes originated in the Labyrinth of Lions. He and Arthur discuss the  content and provenance until at last it becomes apparent, to Timothy's obvious disappointment, that it's a  much more recent forgery.  [Lesson: Inks of Revelation]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.arun.json.startdescription: Reverend Timothy has realised that Arun is the author of 'The Radical Measure', the notorious nineteenth-century manifesto for experimental poetry, and is hanging on Arun's every word: he has almost stopped talking. [Lesson: Preliminal Meter]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.azita.json.startdescription: Azita and Reverend Timothy are discussing the churches of the East - variations on the Solar faith with other hours acknowledged, and hold-outs of the Crucian heresy. (Azita objects mildly to Timothy describing it as the 'Crucian heresy'.) [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.chaima.json.startdescription: Timothy clearly has no idea what to say to Chaima, at least for the first few minutes. At this point he arbitrarily picks aquatic snails as a topic (he is, it seems, a keen amateur naturalist) and for some time he talks to Chaima about aquatic snails. And for some time, Chaima listens to him talk about them. [Lesson: Pearl & Tide]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.connie.json.startdescription: Timothy asks Connie detailed questions about the construction of the Cucurbit, which she answers very guardedly until she realises Timothy's interest is fundamentally architectural and that in fact he mostly seems to have forgotten that it's a prison. [Lesson: Door & Wall]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.coquille.jso.startdescription: Timothy is enthusiastically recounting his previous week's sermon to Coquille, obviously flattered by her interest, although a neutral observer would notice her interest is becoming increasingly glazed and desperate. [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.corso.json.startdescription: Corso has learnt that Reverend Timothy has a tiny library of theological texts inherited from a Welsh maiden aunt, and is manoeuvring to identify whether Timothy has anything of value while also trying to avoid coming across as overly predatory. Fortunately for Corso, Timothy remains oblivious; unfortunately for Timothy and Corso both, the library consists largely of Victorian reprints. [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.dagmar.json.startdescription: Dagmar, complaining about her aching back, launches into a blistering assault on Timothy: she seems to hold him personally responsible, through the Church and ultimately the Madrugad, for the Tally of Years which the Madrugad maintains and which determines mortal lifespans. Timothy bows before the assault like a willow in a storm but nevertheless rehearses the usual moral and theological arguments in the Tally's favour. Dagmar eventually lets slip that she has engaged in 'nectaring and reckoning', apparently adjusting her entry in the Tally, and rather shiftily retires from the argument. [Lesson: Edicts Liminal]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.douglas.json.startdescription: Douglas and Reverend Timothy happily discuss the raising of roses. [Lesson: Leaves & Thorns]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.ehsan.json.startdescription: Timothy takes the opportunity to ask Ehsan about the operations of the Hush House infirmary. His interest is clearly historical, but Ehsan, in a mood of unusual mischief, details some of the more alarming chirurgic operations carried out there in times past, leaving Timothy faintly green... [Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.fraser.json.startdescription: Timothy (a keen amateur naturalist) shares his wasp-related insights with Fraser. Fraser's interest waxes and wanes. [Lesson: Insects & Nectars]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.hokobald.jso.startdescription: Hokobald is pressing Reverend Timothy on the New King - particularly, on the claims by some prelates that he may be associated with the Second Dawn, even though that might seem to conflict with the Received Version of the Book of Suns. Hokobald's aim is clearly malice. Timothy clearly realises this, and he is also clearly quite frightened of Hokobald. He remains polite, although pale and unusually quiet. [Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]
